 Job Description: 
 Department Overview 
 The TD Legal Group is a high-performing and collaborative team of lawyers and legal professionals. Our colleagues are located across Canada, the United States and other jurisdictions in which TD operates. We provide legal advice and support on a broad range of legal, regulatory, governance and strategic matters that support the Bank's businesses, corporate functions and objectives.
 We are looking for a Senior Law Clerk, Board Governance to join our Corporate and Subsidiary Governance Legal team. The successful candidate will work closely with lawyers and other legal professionals to support the effective operation of the Bank's Board of Directors and its Committees.
 Job Overview 
 The Senior Law Clerk will provide experienced corporate governance and law clerk support for the Board and its Committees. The role requires strong judgment, attention to detail and organizational skills, together with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and interact effectively with Directors, senior executives and other stakeholders across TD. The successful candidate will be expected to exercise a high degree of discretion and maintain confidentiality in handling sensitive and confidential matters.
 Job Accountabilities 
 The responsibilities of the Senior Law Clerk may include:
 Supporting the end-to-end administration of Board and Committee meetings, including annual meeting planning and scheduling, preparation of agendas, coordination of meeting materials and meeting-related communications.
 Coordinate with senior executives and other stakeholders to obtain and prepare materials for Board and Committee meetings and ensure applicable requirements and timelines are met.
 Prepare draft agendas, minutes and other Board and Committee records and support the review and finalization of these materials.
 Manage meeting-day processes and logistics and provide support to the Corporate Secretary, the Assistant Corporate Secretary, and other members of the team as required.
 Maintain Board and Committee minute books, records, calendars, trackers, workplans and other governance documentation.
 Manage Board and Committee materials through the Board portal, including posting and distributing materials and related communications to Directors.
 Complete post-meeting activities, including finalization and maintenance of corporate records, follow-up on outstanding matters and preparation of materials for regulatory filing or submission, as required.
 Support the maintenance of Board and Committee governance documents, including mandates, charters, policies, procedures and related materials.
 Apply knowledge of corporate law and governance requirements and practices to support Board and Committee processes and respond to governance-related questions.
 Keep apprised of and support compliance with applicable corporate governance requirements and established Board and Committee processes.
 Prepare, organize and maintain resolutions, memoranda, notices, consents and other corporate and governance documentation.
 Build and maintain strong working relationships with Directors, senior executives and stakeholders across TD and respond to requests in a timely and professional manner.
 Independently manage and prioritize multiple ongoing responsibilities, including matters that may be sensitive, confidential or time-critical.
 Identify opportunities to enhance Board and Committee processes, records management and other governance practices.
 Contribute to other governance and Legal Group initiatives, including knowledge management and process improvement.
 Perform other Board and Committee governance and related law clerk responsibilities as required.
 Job Requirements 
 5+ years of relevant law clerk, paralegal or corporate secretarial experience, preferably with a major financial institution, public company or law firm.
 Experience supporting boards of directors or board committees is strongly preferred.
 Practical knowledge of corporate secretarial requirements and Board and Committee governance practices.
 Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
 Strong judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify issues and determine appropriate next steps.
 Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively as part of a team.
 Demonstrated reliability, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
 Strong interpersonal and relationship-management skills, including the confidence and judgment to interact effectively with Directors, senior executives and stakeholders across the organization.
 Ability to exercise discretion and maintain confidentiality when handling sensitive matters.
 Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
 Experience with Diligent or another Board portal is an asset.
 A proactive, service-oriented approach and commitment to continuous improvement.

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. 
 Lyft is looking for a talented, tech-savvy tax accountant to join our growing Tax Team. As a Senior Tax Analyst, you will report to the Tax Manager and take full ownership of indirect tax accounting, compliance, audit work streams, and from time to time ad hoc projects, delivering actionable insights and recommendations that influence business decisions. You will build trusted relationships across Engineering, Business Operations, Regulatory Compliance, and Accounting/Finance, and serve as a resource and mentor to junior members of the tax team.
 Responsibilities: 
 Tax Technical & Accounting Expertise 
 Ensure accurate application of indirect tax and regulatory laws across assigned areas, reviewing complex tax returns and overseeing the compliance process end-to-end
 Review tax and accounting records for quality and accuracy, identifying and correcting issues before they escalate
 Lead preparation of workpapers and audit defense arguments for indirect tax audits, gathering transaction details and developing well-supported positions for submission to tax authorities
 Train and mentor team members cross-functionally on indirect tax laws, regulatory requirements, and best practices within their area
 Compliance & Reporting 
 Oversee the entire indirect tax compliance process, ensuring all returns, schedules, and related documents are filed accurately and on time across jurisdictions
 Develop strategies to ensure documentation and record-keeping meet audit and regulatory standards
 Gather and analyze data from the general ledger, tax engines, and other systems to lead workpaper preparation for compliance and reverse indirect tax audits
 Coach junior team members on compliance processes and reporting quality
 Tax Strategy & Planning 
 Analyze current and upcoming tax regulations, developing and recommending strategies to ensure ongoing compliance and optimize the company's tax position
 Research complex indirect tax issues and develop clear, actionable guidance for internal business partners
 Identify and assess indirect tax risks (notices, resale/exemption certificate exposure, nexus issues) and lead resolution efforts
 Develop a deep understanding of Lyft's business operations to proactively flag indirect tax implications of new products, markets, or transactions
 Tax Operational Efficiency 
 Lead efforts to streamline and automate indirect tax workflows, including building and maintaining Excel/Alteryx models for recurring transactions and scenarios
 Develop and track performance metrics to measure the efficiency and accuracy of the indirect tax compliance process
 Coordinate with cross-functional teams (Engineering, Business Operations) to ensure system and process changes support indirect tax compliance
 Drive ad hoc process improvement projects related to indirect tax, proposing and implementing solutions independently
 Experience: 
 Bachelor's Degree in Accounting, Tax, or related field with 5+ years of tax accounting experience in either corporate or public accounting
 CA, CPA or CMI designation preferred
 In-depth technical knowledge of laws governing Sales and Use Taxes, Value-added Tax, personal property tax, business licenses/gross receipts tax, and related reporting to tax authorities within the United States, Canada, Europe, Mexico and beyond
 Demonstrated ability to lead complex projects with significant autonomy, proactively identifying risks, opportunities, and process improvements
 Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with experience presenting findings and recommendations to cross-functional and senior stakeholders
 Strong accounting skills, including the ability to independently review and reconcile complex general ledger accounts
 Strong computer and technology skills, including advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel; Alteryx, Python, or SQL experience strongly preferred
 Accounting system experience (Oracle, NetSuite, or similar ERP)
 Tax engine experience (Vertex, OneSource, Avalara, or similar)
 Experience coaching, training, or mentoring team members cross-functionally

 À propos du poste 
 Nous recherchons un(e) Conseiller(ère) Sénior(e) VPO -  Construction, afin de soutenir l’exécution efficace des projets structurants à travers les installations du SLSJ (Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean).
 Relevant du Chef de Service Construction, vous agirez à titre d’expert fonctionnel et de gardien des pratiques VPO** du département. Vous veillerez à élaborer, uniformiser, déployer et améliorer les méthodes, les outils et les processus VPO afin d’assurer une exécution de projets performante, prévisible et conforme aux normes de l’organisation.

Il soutient les équipes de projet dans l'application des méthodes établies, veille à leur conformité et contribue à l'amélioration de la performance globale des projets par l'utilisation efficace des outils et processus VPO.
 ** VPO : La Vérification Pré-Opérationnelle est l'ensemble des activités réalisées après la construction et avant le démarrage officiel de l'installation , afin de confirmer que les systèmes, équipements et sous-systèmes sont correctement installés, fonctionnels et sécuritaires.

 Promouvoir et incarner une culture axée sur la santé et la sécurité, l’inclusion, la performance, la rigueur et l’amélioration continue au sein des équipes.

 Accompagner les équipes de projet dans la mise en place et la mobilisation des équipes VPO.
 Définir les rôles, responsabilités, interfaces et modes de fonctionnement des ressources VPO.
 Soutenir l'intégration des pratiques VPO dès les phases de planification, d'approvisionnement et d'exécution.  Mobiliser et développer les équipes avec une approche alignée sur les valeurs et les objectifs de l’entreprise.
 Définir les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) lié à l’efficacité du plan VPO incluant son exécution. Mettre en place les mécanismes de suivi et veiller à l'intégration des meilleures pratiques. Contribuer activement aux revues de projets, aux analyses de performance et aux recommandations d’actions correctives.
 Conseiller les gestionnaires de projet, les équipes de construction et les entrepreneurs relativement aux stratégies VPO.
 Assurer une collaboration efficace et une gestion rigoureuse de la performance avec les partenaires externes impliqués dans la réalisation de la phase VPO des projets.

(Construction industrielle, mise en service (Commissioning), Vérification pré-opérationnelle (VPO) et démarrage d’installations industrielles.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
 Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
 The Team
 Our Login and MFA team owns the most consequential surface in software: the exact moment someone proves who they are. Getting this right means designing security that's invisible when it works, flows that guide without friction, and experiences that people trust without thinking twice. We're looking for a designer who obsesses over the details that make that possible.
 You'll join a distributed and diverse team of designers who see design as both craft and catalyst. We believe design is never static, it evolves with our users, our products, and our own curiosity. Some days that means diving deep into research and validation, others it's refining existing flows, and often it's imagining bold new ways to move our product forward.
 Our team thrives on collaboration and feedback. We learn from one another, challenge ourselves to raise the bar, and create space to experiment and grow. Designers here have real ownership, influencing product direction alongside engineering and product management while shaping experiences that reach millions of people worldwide.
 If you're energized by complex problems, motivated to push boundaries, and eager to hone your craft while making a lasting impact, this is the place to do it.
 The Role
 As a Staff Product Designer, you'll tackle some of the hardest design challenges in identity: making authentication seamless for end users while remaining powerful and configurable for the developers who build on it. You'll lead design across Auth0's key login and multi factor authentication flows by guiding strategy and raising the craft.
 What you'll be doing
 When everyone on the team can generate UI, the designer's role shifts. You become the person responsible for strong systems thinking, taste, quality, experience, and being the voice of the customer. You hold the quality bar when speed is pushing everything toward "fine."
 Prototype at volume: Use AI tools and code to explore dozens of directions fast, then narrow based on what works and what solves the actual problem. The artifacts you create will be functional and inclusive of all Auth0 developer interfaces.
 Simplify complexity: Shape intuitive, scalable experiences for our customers with high standards for security and composability. You'll be designing customization journeys that make secure and frictionless authentication seamless.
 Raise the craft: Help the broader design org see what this way of working looks like in practice. We're all figuring this out together. You'll take pride in expanding your contributions through code and research-driven insights.
 What you'll bring to the role
 You have craft: This matters most. Considered typography, intentional spacing, polished micro-interactions, details that show someone genuinely cared. We're looking for someone with a refined sense of design taste and a deep appreciation for the details that create a polished, trustworthy experience.
 You build: You've established a mature AI workflow that helps you bring ideas to life quickly. Instead of letting the backlog of small design debt collect, you take action and fix things directly in code.
 You have a real AI practice: Not experimentation, but an actual workflow. You have opinions about where AI tools help and where they fall short.
 You simplify: Auth0 is a robust and composable product. It is your job to create clarity and moments of magic amidst the complexity.
 Note for when applying
 In your application, please include a link to your portfolio with password (if protected). We prioritize a review of your design craft and any examples of your work in code.

 Durham Region | Pickering, Ajax, Whitby, Oshawa, Courtice & Bowmanville 
 The Care Company is a home healthcare company whose purpose is to create A Better Life for Those at Home. We help individuals remain safely and comfortably in their homes for as long as they choose, and our real talent is helping people Make Each Day Count. We are a company that puts People First and strives to get Better Today.
 We are currently looking for compassionate, dependable, and self-driven Registered Nurses (RNs) and Registered Practical Nurses (RPNs) to support pediatric and young adult clients throughout Durham Region, including Pickering, Ajax, Whitby, Oshawa, Courtice, and Bowmanville.
 Our nurses provide one-to-one nursing care in home, school, and community settings to clients with varying levels of medical complexity.
 Pediatric nursing experience is required, and previous complex-care experience is a strong asset. We are willing to provide additional training to the right candidates who have a strong pediatric or community nursing foundation and are interested in developing their complex-care skills. 
 We are currently seeking nurses to support two of our community-based paediatric clients: 
 1) School support for 10 y/o female in Oshawa Mondays-Fridays (must commit to all days) 8am-4pm (client requires bus accompaniment to and from school)
 2) Home care for 2 y/o male client in Pickering Wednesdays-Sundays day shifts 12pm-4pm; also seeking overnight coverage 11pm-7am Mon/Tues/Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun *Must be able to do at least 3 shifts/week to be considered* 
 Scheduling
 Consistent, ongoing weekly availability is required. Nurses must be able to commit to the same agreed-upon shift(s), on the same day(s), each week. 
 Continuity of care is extremely important to our clients and families, and we prioritize nurses who are interested in developing long-term relationships with their clients. 
 Opportunities may include daytime, evening, overnight, weekday, and weekend shifts depending on current client needs and nurse availability. 
 What You'll Do
 Provide safe, compassionate, one-to-one nursing care in accordance with each client's individualized care plan and medical orders. 
 Complete ongoing nursing assessments and monitor clients for changes in respiratory, neurological, physical, cognitive, and overall clinical status. 
 Provide complex nursing interventions within your scope of practice and demonstrated competency, which may include tracheostomy care, suctioning, respiratory support, enteral feeding, seizure management, medication administration, and other client-specific interventions. 
 Recognize and respond appropriately to changes in client condition and promptly escalate concerns when required. 
 Respond appropriately to urgent or emergency situations in the home, school, or community setting. 
 Support clients with activities of daily living, mobility, transfers, personal care, and other needs outlined in their individualized care plans. 
 Safely operate client-specific medical and mobility equipment in accordance with training and the client's plan of care. 
 Collaborate with clients, families, school personnel, physicians, Ontario Health atHome, and other members of the interdisciplinary care team. 
 Maintain accurate, complete, and timely clinical documentation in accordance with CNO standards and The Care Company policies. 
 Practice safely and competently within your individual knowledge, skill, judgment, training, and professional scope of practice. 
 Pediatric & Complex Care Experience
 Candidates must have pediatric nursing experience, ideally with hands-on experience in one or more of the following:
 Tracheostomy care and suctioning 
 Ventilator support 
 G-tube and J-tube feeding and care 
 BiPAP or CPAP 
 Cough assist 
 Oxygen therapy and respiratory monitoring 
 Seizure monitoring and management 
 Don't have experience with every intervention listed above? We are willing to train the right candidates!
 We encourage nurses with a strong pediatric or community nursing background to apply, even if they are still developing some of their complex-care competencies. Client-specific orientation and training may be provided based on the needs of the assignment.
 Previous experience working in home and community care or supporting Ontario Health atHome (formerly HCCSS) clients is also a strong asset.
 Other Requirements
 Current registration and good standing with the College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO) as an RN or RPN. 
 Valid nursing certificate/registration. 
 Current CPR and First Aid certification. 
 Valid WHMIS 2015 certification completed within the past 12 months. 
 Negative TB test completed within the past 12 months. 
 Valid Criminal Record Check with Vulnerable Sector Screening completed within the past 12 months. 
 COVID-19 vaccination documentation, subject to accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code. 
 Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing. 
 Strong nursing assessment, critical-thinking, communication, and clinical judgment skills. 
 Ability to identify and promptly report client care concerns and changes in condition to the appropriate Care Coordinator or healthcare provider. 
 Ability to work independently in home, school, and community environments while collaborating with the broader healthcare team. 
 A valid driver's licence and reliable access to a vehicle is an asset but not required. 
 Why Join The Care Company? 
 Competitive hourly rates: 
 RPN: $36.25/hour-$40.25/hour 
 RN: $47.75/hour-$50.75/hour 
 Opportunities for consistent, ongoing client assignments. 
 One-to-one nursing care, allowing you to focus on the individual needs of your client. 
 24/7 nursing oversight and clinical support. 
 Client-specific orientation and training opportunities. 
 Educational and professional development opportunities. 
 PPE provided. 
 Employee Recognition Program. 
 Health and Wellness Program. 
 Opportunities to further develop your pediatric and complex-care nursing skills. 
 The Care Company is committed to providing accommodations throughout the recruitment and onboarding process. Please let us know if you require accommodation or additional assistance. 
 Thank you to everyone who applies. Due to the volume of applications received, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

Media buying is now the easy part. 
 In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.
 So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.
 Here's what "end to end" actually means here.
 You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.
 You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.
 You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 We're growing fast and we keep the bar high. 
 We believe the best media buyer today is a sharp marketer who uses AI every day. We built an internal creative analysis tool that connects to Claude, and we use Pipeboard to read and write to ad accounts and run heavy analysis. You don't need to know our stack yet. You do need to actually use AI in your work, not be afraid of it, and teach yourself what you don't know.
 What the job looks like
 Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
 Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
 Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.
 Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
 Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
 Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
 You're a fit if
 You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
 You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
 You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
 You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
 You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
 You're not a fit if
 "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 Why This Role Is Exciting
 This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets.  We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You will grow into senior strategy.  We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!







ROLE OVERVIEW

We're seeking a senior product leader to own Cohere's Inference as a Service business end to end. The product is sovereign, self-serve inference: a mid-market or enterprise buyer picks a model, a region and a GPU size, and is running the same afternoon with no procurement cycle and no infrastructure of their own. You'll decide which open-weights and first-party models we serve, in which regions and on which hardware, set the rate card they sell at, and carry the revenue and margin that follow from those calls. You own the platform around that endpoint as well, from the console and dashboards a customer administers their deployment through to the catalog of first-party and third-party models behind it.

You'll set the strategy and run the execution, which means choosing where to spend across serving efficiency, the self-serve console and regional capacity when all three want the same budget, and shipping the deployment framework that removes infrastructure barriers while holding the line on data residency, compliance and operational confidence. You'll do that across engineering, serving, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority over most of it, and you'll be accountable for the outcome rather than for the roadmap.

The timing is most of the opportunity. Every serious company is deciding where its models will run and what it costs to keep them running, serving demand is climbing faster than anyone can rack hardware for it, and very few of those buyers are willing to hand their data to an operator who can read it. We are starting this business from a standing start, with the models, the silicon and the encryption already in place and almost no one else able to offer the combination. You would be taking a product to market in the window where that advantage is still ours, building one of Cohere's major revenue lines from its first customer onward, and shaping how a generation of companies buys AI it can actually trust.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the P&L for Inference as a Service: carry the revenue number, set the rate card, and keep blended margin above the floor as the catalog and the fleet grow.

 - Own the inference platform itself: the console and dashboards where customers see usage, spend, API keys, access control and attestation, and the value-add tooling that makes a managed endpoint worth more than a raw one.

 - Own the model inventory across first-party and third-party models: what enters the catalog, how it is grouped by provenance, what it is priced at, and when something is quantised, replaced or retired.

 - Set the roadmap and the investment case across serving efficiency, the self-serve surface and regional capacity, and make the call when those three compete for the same budget.

 - Build the commercial motion with GTM from the ground up: self-serve acquisition for the mid-market, a sales-led motion for enterprise, and the partnerships that monetise capacity we would otherwise leave idle.

 - Stay close to the market: talk to customers and developers about integration friction and unmet needs, track competitor pricing, catalogs and launches, and follow where models and hardware are heading, then turn that into a clear view of where we should place our bets and what it would take to win.

 - Define the metrics that tell us whether this is a business, including revenue, margin, win rate, time to first token and self-serve share, and lead the work that moves them.

 - Partner with engineering, research, legal, finance, technical writing and developer relations to ship the platform and clear the licensing, pricing and capacity decisions behind it.

 - Represent the business to the executive team with a recommendation, the evidence behind it and the trade-off it implies.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 10+ years of product management experience, including meaningful time owning a B2B infrastructure or platform product at the scope of a business rather than a feature area.

 - Experience operating in a GM-like capacity: you have carried a revenue line or a P&L, set pricing, and been held to margin as well as to shipping.

 - Background at a neocloud such as Together AI, Baseten or Fireworks, or at a hyperscaler such as AWS, Azure, OCI or Google Cloud, with a working view of how inference capacity is priced, packaged and sold, and a point of view on where the segment goes next.

 - A track record of thinking about infrastructure as a product, with the ability to translate system-level capabilities into clearly differentiated, customer-facing features.

 - Entrepreneurial, with experience taking a new product to market and building the commercial motion around it rather than inheriting one.

 - Experience with deployment models such as multi-tenant and dedicated infrastructure, and ownership across the full product lifecycle, from problem definition through launch, iteration and eventual migration or deprecation.

 - Analytical by default: you define success metrics before you build, instrument thoughtfully, and use data alongside qualitative feedback to make decisions.

 - Able to set direction and earn alignment across engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority, and to put a clear recommendation and its trade-offs in front of an executive audience.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience owning a model serving or inference platform, including self-serve infrastructure and metered inference offerings.

 - Exposure to data residency, sovereignty, or regional compliance requirements as they apply to AI or cloud infrastructure products, particularly in the inference-as-a-service context.

 - Familiarity with the AI developer ecosystem and open standards, including orchestration frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex, model serving frameworks such as vLLM, and an awareness of de facto interoperability standards and how they shape developer adoption and integration patterns for inference workloads.

 - Experience with GPU infrastructure and cloud deployment models across both neocloud and hyperscaler environments.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

About Gramian 
Gramian Consultancy is a boutique consultancy specializing in IT professional services and engineering talent solutions. With a strong background in software engineering and leadership, we help companies build high-performing teams by matching them with professionals who truly fit their needs.
 About the Job 
We are seeking highly skilled Aerodynamics and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) Specialists with strong programming capabilities to contribute to a specialized AI training project focused on aerodynamic analysis, engineering simulation, and Python-based computational workflows.
 This role is particularly suited to engineers who combine a solid understanding of fluid mechanics and applied aerodynamics with practical software development and coding skills. You will create, solve, review, and validate engineering tasks using programmatic, command-line-based workflows.
 Typical assignments may involve analyzing airfoils, preparing computational domains and meshes, defining boundary conditions, running CFD simulations, calculating lift and drag, and validating whether resulting flow fields are numerically stable and physically realistic.
 Practical coding ability is essential. We are looking for engineers who can actively write Python code, automate engineering workflows, and work with computational tools—not simply candidates who hold relevant academic degrees without the ability to implement technical solutions.
 Previous AI experience is not required.
 LOCATION: Remote – US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, UK, Southeast Asia, and APAC
 WORKLOAD: Approximately 15 hours per week.
 SCHEDULE: Flexible; choose your working days and hours, including weekends.
 COMPENSATION MODEL: Output-based, with payment per task that meets project specifications.
 PROJECT: AI training focused on aerodynamics, CFD, engineering simulation, and Python.
 AI EXPERIENCE: Not required.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Solve and validate complex aerodynamic and fluid dynamics problems.
 Translate physical engineering requirements into computational models and solver-ready cases.
 Create or modify geometries, computational domains, and meshes.
 Define appropriate initial conditions, boundary conditions, fluid properties, and solver settings.
 Execute CFD and aerodynamic analysis workflows using command-line-accessible tools.
 Write Python code to automate preprocessing, simulation execution, parameter sweeps, postprocessing, and validation.
 Develop scripts and computational workflows for engineering analysis.
 Calculate and interpret aerodynamic quantities, including lift, drag, pressure distributions, and flow characteristics.
 Evaluate mesh quality, numerical convergence, solver stability, and physical validity of simulation results.
 Diagnose non-convergence, unstable solutions, incorrect results, and physically invalid outputs.
 Select and justify modeling assumptions, mesh strategies, boundary conditions, and solver configurations.
 Document technical methodologies, engineering decisions, and simulation results.
 Candidates should meet one of the following educational pathways:
 Pathway 1: Master's or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering with a specialization in aerodynamics, fluid dynamics, or thermofluids.
 Pathway 2: Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering or Mechanical Engineering, combined with at least 1–2 years of relevant aerodynamics-specific professional or research experience.
 Additional requirements:
 Strong understanding of fluid mechanics and applied aerodynamics.
 Practical experience formulating and executing CFD or aerodynamic analyses.
 Strong practical proficiency in Python, including the ability to write and debug code independently.
 Experience using Python for scientific computing, engineering automation, or computational analysis.
 Experience with at least one engineering tool or library accessible through a command-line interface, scripting interface, configuration files, or programmatic API.
 Ability to select and justify modeling assumptions, boundary conditions, mesh strategies, and solver settings.
 Ability to diagnose numerical convergence issues, unstable solutions, and physically invalid results.
 Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
 Ability to communicate technical reasoning and engineering trade-offs clearly.
 Professional English proficiency at C1 level or higher.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!



Role Overview:

As a Performance Engineer in the Pre-Training team you will be responsible for optimizing the performance of our advanced language models and systems. Their primary focus is on improving key model training metrics, such as training throughput, ensuring high accelerator utilization.

The team combines expertise in software engineering, machine learning, and low-level kernel design and development to design robust systems and enhance model performance. You will work on identifying and removing performance bottlenecks, develop cutting-edge training and profiling tools to help Cohere's mission of providing efficient and reliable language understanding and generation capabilities and drive innovation in the field of natural language processing.

Note: We have offices in London, Toronto, New York and San Francisco, but we’re also remote-friendly! This team operates primarily between ET to CET time zones, so we’re seeking candidates in locations that align with these hours for effective collaboration.



Key Responsibilities:

 - Design and write high-performant and scalable software for training. 

 - Understand architectural modifications and design choices and their effects on training throughput and quality.

 - Write low-level CUDA, triton kernels to squeeze every last bit of performance from our accelerators.

 - Research, implement, and experiment with ideas on our supercompute and data infrastructure.

 - Learn from and work with the best researchers in the field.



Qualifications:

 - Extremely strong software engineering skills.

 - Proficiency in Python and related ML frameworks such as JAX, Pytorch and XLA/MLIR.

 - Experience writing kernels for GPUs using CUDA, triton, etc

 - Experience using large-scale distributed training strategies.

 - Familiarity with autoregressive sequence models, such as Transformers.

Bonus: paper at top-tier venues (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AIStats, MLSys, JMLR, AAAI, Nature, COLING, ACL, EMNLP).



Working location:

This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.





FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

The Company 
 Versaterm is a PE-backed, high-growth SaaS company building a fully integrated platform across the entire public safety ecosystem — dispatch, law enforcement, forensics, courts, and beyond . We've grown through strategic acquisitions and deep product investment. What connects all of it is a single purpose: give public safety agencies the tools and insights to make better decisions in high-stakes moments. 
 When a 911 call is answered, a detective investigates a case, or a forensic lab processes evidence, there's a good chance our software is working behind the scenes. That's been true for over four decades. 
 AI is central to where we're going. Not as a feature but as core infrastructure. We're embedding intelligence directly into the workflows our customers rely on every day, and we're doing it alongside them. Our customers tell us what the mission demands. We build what answers it. 
 This work attracts a specific kind of person — someone who wants to be pushed by great people, build things that outlast a sprint cycle, and go home knowing the work connected back to something real. 
 The Role 
 The Director of Customer Success leads the post-sale customer lifecycle across all customer segments, ensuring customers realize measurable value, adopt solutions effectively, and renew and expand over time. This role is accountable for building and scaling a high-performing Customer Success organization operating under a “One Account, One Owner” model, with clear ownership of customer outcomes across Strategic, Enterprise, State, and Transactional accounts. 
 The Director defines how Customer Success operates—establishing engagement models, operating cadence, and cross-functional alignment—while ensuring consistent execution across the core pillars of Strategic Engagement, Adoption, Expansion, and Retention. The role partners closely with Sales, Project Delivery/Onboarding, Support, Product, and Marketing to deliver a seamless and scalable customer experience. 
 This job posting is being used to fill an existing vacancy.

 Customer Success Strategy & Execution 
 Execute Customer Success strategies across all customer segments, ensuring alignment to company growth and retention objectives. 
 Establish standardized customer lifecycle motions, including success planning, business reviews, adoption programs, and renewal readiness. 
 Ensure a proactive, outcome-driven approach to customer engagement focused on value realization and measurable impact. 
 Build scalable processes and playbooks that reduce duplication and ensure consistency across Customer Success teams. 
 Operating Model & Segmentation 
 Lead a multi-tier engagement model across Strategic, State, Enterprise, and Transactional accounts. 
 Operationalize a hub-and-spoke model, where Customer Success Managers own relationships and provide general project knowledge and engage specialists for additional targeted support.

 Leading the Renewals team and partnering with sales teams to drive expansion opportunities and maximize lifetime value.

 Proven experience owning retention, renewals, and customer growth metrics at scale.

About Clutch: 
 We’re on a mission to reinvent the way Canadians buy and sell cars. Clutch combines an intuitive online experience with in-house vehicle reconditioning, logistics and financial services to make buying or selling a car simpler, more transparent and more convenient, all backed by our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee.
 Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Toronto, Clutch serves customers across Ontario, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island. We generate over $1 billion in annual revenue and have been named to The Globe and Mail’s list of Canada’s Top Growing Companies for six consecutive years, along with Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50™ and Fast 500™. We’re backed by world-class investors including D1 Capital, Altos Ventures, BMO Capital Partners, Canaan and Real Ventures.
 We’ve reached meaningful scale, and we’re still early in our ambition to become a household name in Canadian automotive retail. That’s where you come in: we’re looking for curious, hard-working, driven people who want to build it with us. Learn more at clutch.ca.
 The Opportunity 
 We’re hiring a Director of Strategic Partnerships to build a new commercial growth function from the ground up. Your mission: unlock scalable, profitable ways for Canadians to buy from and sell to Clutch through relationships and programs that neither company could build as effectively alone.
 You’ll identify opportunities across vehicle supply, customer distribution and reciprocal customer benefits, and work with our Brand team on select high-impact brand partnerships. We’ve already had success here — brand partnerships with the Toronto Raptors and the NBA, supply partnerships with OEMs like Tesla — and we’re investing heavily behind the strategy. Think a leasing company making it easier for its customers to sell their current vehicle, a financial institution or fleet operator creating a better path to vehicle disposition, a national service network introducing Clutch to relevant buyers and sellers, or an insurance partner simplifying the car-purchase journey. These are illustrative examples, not existing partnerships.
 This is a builder’s role, not a sponsorship or account-management position. You’ll find the opportunity, build the business case, win the partner, negotiate the economics, lead the launch and keep improving the relationship. Reporting directly to our CFO & Head of Marketing, you’ll have the autonomy and executive access to make meaningful deals happen — and the opportunity to build a team as the function scales.
 What You’ll Do 
 Set the strategy. Map the highest-potential partnership categories, size the commercial upside and prioritize the opportunities with the best incremental economics and clearest path to execution.
 Unlock new vehicle supply. Originate programs with OEMs, direct-to-consumer automotive brands, lenders, leasing and fleet companies, and others that control or influence trade-ins and disposition — working with internal teams to route each channel to the right retail or wholesale outcome.
 Build new customer distribution channels. Partner with banks, insurers, membership and loyalty programs, automotive-service networks and other consumer businesses to reach high-intent buyers and sellers at the right moment, through referral programs, embedded customer journeys, co-marketing and partner-funded benefits.
 Support brand partnerships. Work alongside Brand Marketing, who owns our sports, cultural and consumer-brand relationships, contributing commercial structure and partner-development expertise where there’s distribution or customer-value upside. 
 Own the deal end to end. Run a disciplined pipeline from outbound outreach through executive conversations, deal modelling, commercial terms and contracting. Lead cross-functional launches with Marketing, Brand, Product, Vehicle Acquisition, Operations, Finance, Legal and Customer Experience.
 Grow what you launch. Act as the commercial owner for key relationships: track activation, resolve issues, lead business reviews and expand or renew the partnerships that perform. The work doesn’t stop at signature.
 Build a repeatable function. Measure real impact — incremental vehicles acquired, qualified leads, transactions, cost to acquire, contribution profit and clear reach and engagement goals for brand-led work — and codify what works into evaluation criteria, scorecards and launch playbooks. Recruit and develop a team as the opportunity scales.
 What Success Looks Like 
 Within your first year, you’ve built a credible pipeline of strategically valuable relationships and launched multiple operating partnerships delivering measurable, incremental vehicles, customers or brand value. You’ve earned trusted senior relationships, proven which partnership models scale profitably, and created a repeatable system for finding, closing, launching and growing partnerships, without compromising our brand, customer experience or vehicle quality.
 What You Bring 
 8+ years in business development, strategic partnerships or related commercial roles , with a track record of independently leading complex opportunities. Exceptional candidates with different career paths are welcome.
 Proof you’ve done this before. You’ve personally originated, negotiated, launched and grown partnerships that delivered measurable commercial results — and you’re comfortable prospecting, building a qualified pipeline and closing.
 Strong commercial judgement. You can build a financial case, evaluate unit economics, test incrementality and recognize when a deal looks better on paper than in practice.
 Executive presence. Excellent relationship-building and negotiation skills, and the ability to influence leaders inside and outside the company.
 Exceptional follow-through. You can coordinate a multi-team launch, handle setbacks and stay accountable for performance after the deal is signed.
 Builder’s independence. The curiosity and resourcefulness to stand up a function without a pre-existing team or step-by-step direction.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience in consumer marketplaces, embedded finance or insurance, digital commerce, loyalty and membership ecosystems, or platform partnerships.
 Exposure to automotive retail, remarketing, leasing, fleet, lending or insurance.
 Experience building a partnerships team or launching a new business line.
 Why Clutch 
 Real scale, real momentum. Join a $1B+ business that’s still growing fast and reimagining one of Canada’s largest consumer categories.
 Build something that’s yours. Establish a new commercial function, shape its strategy, personally close flagship deals and build the team as it grows.
 A direct seat at the table. Work closely with the CFO & Head of Marketing and other senior executives, with the autonomy to move quickly and make a visible, company-wide impact.
 Meaningful ownership. Share in the value you help create through equity opportunities.
 Comprehensive benefits from day one. Health, dental, vision, prescription, life insurance and dependent coverage for eligible permanent full-time employees.
 Employment Type: New Vacancy, Permanent Full-Time
 Compensation & Benefits: 
 Benefits: Comprehensive healthcare, dental, vision, prescriptions, life insurance, and dependent coverage; starting from day 1.
 Pay decisions reflect skills, performance, market benchmarking, responsibilities, and working conditions.

 Owning outcomes and finishing work without being chased.

Reference Number: R2873011
 Position Title: Medical Director One Rare
 Department: Medical Specialty Care Canada
 Location: Toronto, Ontario (Hybrid)
 About Sanofi 
 We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives. 
About the Job 
 Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you’ll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.​ 
The Medical Director One Rare is a senior medical leader within the Sanofi Specialty Care Canada Medical Affairs team. This individual will define and drive the medical strategy and execution for both the Rare Diseases and Rare Blood Disorders therapeutic areas in Canada. As a people leader, they will manage and inspire a medical team serving as a coach, mentor, and champion for their team's growth and impact.
 This role sits at the intersection of science, strategy, and humanity. The Medical Director, One Rare will be the Canadian medical voice for some of the most complex and meaningful conditions in medicine — partnering with rare disease and rare blood disorders specialists, payers, and regulators to ensure that every eligible patient in Canada has access to the best possible care. This is a role for a leader who is as passionate about people — patients, caregivers, and team members alike — as they are about science.
 For more than 40 years, Sanofi has dedicated itself to patients, families, and healthcare providers navigating the extraordinary challenges of diagnosing and managing rare conditions. With over 7,000 known rare diseases affecting 400 million patients and their families worldwide, the need for innovation, compassion, and relentless commitment has never been greater.
 Within Sanofi Specialty Care, our One Rare franchise brings together our Rare Diseases and Rare Blood Disorders portfolios under a unified, patient-first vision: "We help enable fulfilling futures for extraordinary people, no matter how rare their condition." We listen to and learn from patients and their families. Their voices shape our science, our strategies, and our purpose.
 Main responsibilities: 
 A. Medical Strategy & Leadership 
 Define and lead the Canadian medical affairs strategy for Rare Diseases and Rare Blood Disorders, aligned with global and regional priorities
 Develop and execute the Medical Affairs Plan (MAP) for all assigned therapeutic areas within the One Rare portfolio
 Serve as the primary Canadian medical expert and scientific voice for the One Rare franchise, representing Sanofi's scientific leadership internally and externally
 Contribute to lifecycle management strategies, pipeline development, and launch readiness activities for current and future rare disease and rare blood disorder assets
 Provide strategic medical input into brand planning, market access strategies, and reimbursement submissions
 Support the development of diagnostic and treatment pathways to improve early identification, timely diagnosis, and optimal management of patients living with rare and ultra-rare conditions
 Build and maintain trusted, long-term relationships with our partners
 B. People Leadership & Team Management 
 Lead, coach, and develop a team of direct reports covering both Rare Diseases and Rare Blood Disorders across Canada
 Set clear, meaningful objectives aligned with medical and organizational priorities; provide regular, constructive feedback and support the career development and growth of each team member
 Foster a high-performance, inclusive, and deeply patient-centric team culture grounded in empathy, scientific rigor, and shared purpose
 Manage team resources, workload allocation, and performance reviews with fairness and transparency
 Champion a culture of compassion and deep understanding of the patient and caregiver journey — recognizing that in rare diseases, every patient counts and every interaction matters
 C. Scientific Engagement & External Stakeholder Management 
 Build and maintain trusted, long-term relationships with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), rare disease specialists, metabolic disease centers, hemophilia treatment centers (HTCs), academic institutions, patient advocacy groups, and healthcare professionals across Canada
 Lead and support advisory boards, scientific symposia, medical education initiatives, and patient/caregiver education programs
 Represent Sanofi at national and international medical congresses, rare disease forums, hemophilia conferences, and patient advocacy events
 Engage with Health Canada, Canadian Blood Services, CDA, INESSS, and provincial payer bodies on scientific and medical matters relevant to the One Rare portfolio
 Partner closely with rare disease and hemophilia patient advocacy organizations to ensure the patient and caregiver voice is meaningfully integrated into medical strategy and decision-making
 D. Evidence Generation & Data Dissemination 
 Oversee the design and execution of local evidence generation activities, including investigator-initiated trials (IITs), patient registries, real-world evidence (RWE) studies, and patient-reported outcomes (PRO) research
 Support Canadian participation in global rare disease registries and natural history studies
 Ensure timely, accurate, and compliant dissemination of clinical and scientific data to relevant stakeholders
 Review and approve medical content — including publications, scientific slide decks, medical information responses, and patient/caregiver materials — for scientific accuracy, balance, and compliance
E. Cross-Functional Collaboration 
 Partner closely with Commercial, Market Access, Regulatory, Patient Safety, and Patient Advocacy teams to ensure integrated, patient-focused strategies across the One Rare portfolio
 Collaborate with global and regional Medical Affairs teams to align on priorities, contribute Canadian insights, and leverage global scientific resources
 Provide medical and scientific guidance to support reimbursement submissions, health technology assessments (HTAs), and compassionate/special access programs for rare disease patients
 Work with cross-functional teams to optimize patient support programs, access pathways, and continuity of care initiatives
 F. Compliance & Governance 
 Ensure all medical activities comply with Sanofi's internal policies, Health Canada regulations, Innovative Medicines Canada Code of Ethical Practices, and all applicable laws and guidelines
 Champion a culture of ethics, integrity, patient safety, and transparency within the team and across all external engagements
 Ensure adherence to pharmacovigilance requirements and timely reporting of adverse events in accordance with Sanofi's safety obligations
 G. Distributor Partnership & Medical Oversight 
  In the rare disease and rare blood disorder space, Sanofi partners with specialized distributors who play a critical role in ensuring patients receive timely access to complex therapies. Given the highly specialized nature of these medicines robust medical oversight of distributor partnerships is essential to safeguard patient safety, ensure scientific accuracy, and maintain the highest standards of care.
 Serve as the primary medical point of contact for distributor partnerships related to rare disease and rare blood disorder medicines in Canada
 Act as the key medical liaison between Sanofi and our distributor, serving as the medical bridge between both organizations to ensure aligned medical strategies, consistent scientific communication, and optimal patient access
 Provide medical oversight and guidance to distribution partners to ensure consistent, accurate, and compliant medical information and support across all interactions with healthcare professionals and patients
 Collaborate with distributors on medical education, training, and scientific communication activities to ensure alignment with Sanofi's medical strategy and standards
 Review and approve medical content and materials developed by or for distribution partners, ensuring scientific accuracy, balance, and compliance with Health Canada regulations and Innovative Medicines Canada guidelines
 Ensure alignment of medical strategies and messaging between Sanofi and distribution partners, particularly in the context of rare disease treatment protocols and patient management guidelines
 Support distributor partners in addressing medical inquiries, adverse event reporting, and pharmacovigilance requirements, ensuring timely and compliant escalation in accordance with Sanofi's safety obligations
 Monitor and evaluate the quality of medical support provided through distributor partnerships, identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and capability building
 Facilitate knowledge transfer and capability building with distributor medical teams, ensuring they are equipped to support healthcare professionals and patients with the scientific rigor and compassion that rare disease communities deserve
 About you 
 Required Qualifications: 
 MD, PhD, PharmD, or equivalent advanced scientific/medical degree
 Minimum 5-8 years of experience in pharmaceutical/biotech industry with at least 7 years in medical affairs, medical education, or related fields
 Demonstrated experience in Rare Diseases and/or Rare Blood Disorders therapeutic areas (e.g., hemophilia, lysosomal storage disorders, metabolic diseases, or other rare conditions)
 Proven people management experience with a track record of building, developing, and inspiring high-performing teams
 Deep understanding of the Canadian rare disease landscape, including Health Canada regulations, HTA processes (CDA, INESSS), provincial reimbursement pathways, and patient access challenges specific to rare and ultra-rare conditions
 Strong scientific acumen with the ability to translate complex rare disease data into clear, actionable medical strategies
 Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to connect meaningfully with diverse audiences — including specialists, patient advocates, payers, and regulators
 Proven experience working with external partners from a distribution model
 Bilingualism (English/French) is a strong asset given the Canadian market context
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Experience working with hemophilia treatment centers (HTCs) or rare disease centers of excellence
 Knowledge of enzyme replacement therapies, substrate reduction therapies, gene therapies, or other novel rare disease modalities
 Experience with patient registries, natural history studies, or real-world evidence generation in rare disease settings
 Familiarity with compassionate access programs and special access pathways in Canada
 Key Competencies and Skills: 
 Matrix Leadership and Influence: Exceptional ability to lead, influence, and drive results without direct authority — navigating complex organizational structures to achieve objectives through persuasion, credibility, and strategic relationship-building.
 Scientific Leadership: The ability to guide teams and decisions using deep scientific expertise, staying current with medical evidence and translating complex data into actionable insights.
 Strategic Thinking: The capacity to anticipate trends, set long-term priorities, and align medical affairs activities with broader organizational and therapeutic area goals.
 People Leadership & Coaching: The ability to inspire, develop, and empower team members through mentorship, feedback, and creating an environment where individuals can grow and perform at their best.
 Stakeholder Engagement: Building and maintaining productive relationships with key internal and external stakeholders — including KOLs, payers, and regulators — to advance shared objectives.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration: Working effectively across departments (e.g., commercial, regulatory, clinical) to align strategies, share knowledge, and deliver integrated solutions.
 Patient & Caregiver Centricity: Keeping the needs, experiences, and outcomes of patients and their caregivers at the center of every decision, strategy, and interaction.
 Empathy & Compassion: Demonstrating genuine understanding and care for the emotions and perspectives of colleagues, patients, and partners to foster trust and psychological safety.
 Compliance & Ethics: Upholding the highest standards of integrity, transparency, and regulatory compliance in all professional activities and decision-making.
 Data Insights & Evidence Generation: The ability to design, interpret, and communicate real-world evidence and clinical data to support medical strategies and inform healthcare decisions.
 Advocacy & Influence: Championing important causes — for patients, science, or the organization — and persuading stakeholders through credible, evidence-based communication.
 Travel: 
 Approximately 30-40% travel, including domestic and international travel to attend congresses, advisory boards, educational events, and internal leadership forums
 Why choose us? 
 Bring the miracles of science to life alongside a supportive, future-focused team.​ 
 Discover endless opportunities to grow your talent and drive your career, whether it’s through a promotion or lateral move, at home or internationally.​ 
 Enjoy a thoughtful, well-crafted rewards package that recognizes your contribution and amplifies your impact.​ 
 Take good care of yourself and your family, with a wide range of health and wellbeing benefits including high-quality healthcare, prevention and wellness programs​ 
 What Sanofi Offers 
 🚀 Shape the future of digital medical affairs at a leading pharmaceutical company
 💡 Work with cutting-edge technologies — AI, and next-gen digital health platforms
 🤝 Collaborate in an innovative, inclusive environment that values bold ideas
 📈 Grow your career through robust development programs and North American exposure

About Moment Energy 
 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact. 
 We were told second-life batteries would never be safe enough or scalable enough. We didn’t argue, we engineered the solution. Today, Moment Energy delivers 5x the energy density and holds the certifications required to deploy energy independence at scale. 
 Now is the moment. Join us. 
 The Opportunity 
 The Sales Operations Specialist plays a key role to support the effectiveness and growth of our Business Development team. This role sits at the center of our commercial organization, working closely with Account Managers, Application Engineers, and Leadership to improve sales processes, manage our CRM systems, track performance metrics, and ensure smooth coordination across the sales funnel. 
 The Sales Operations Specialist will play a key role in building scalable systems and processes as Moment Energy expands its clean energy storage solutions across North America. 
 Responsibilities 
 Sales Process & Pipeline Management 
 Manage, maintain and implement improvements into the company’s CRM system to ensure accurate pipeline tracking, robust data hygiene, and clear tracking and reporting of essential pipeline performance metrics. 
 Support Account Managers in managing opportunities, updating deal stages, and maintaining customer records. 
 Prepare guides and training materials on usage of the CRM and SOPs for effective funnel management; coach team members on proper usage to ensure CRM data hygiene. 
 Monitor sales pipeline health and provide regular reporting on deal progression, conversion rates, and revenue forecasting. 
 Identify inefficiencies in the sales process and opportunities for improvement in our CRM system’s implementation; implement improvements to increase team productivity. 
 Reporting & Analytics 
 Develop dashboards and reports to track sales performance, pipeline metrics, and key KPIs. 
 Support leadership with forecasting, pipeline analysis, and strategic insights. 
 Track lead sources and campaign effectiveness to inform business development strategy. 
 Identify and report on other insights provided by our CRM data with recommendations on potential improvements to our processes. 
 Cross-Functional Coordination 
 Facilitate and support coordination between Business Development, Application Engineering, Marketing, and Operations. 
 Help ensure customer opportunities move smoothly from early engagement through technical evaluation and contracting. 
 Support proposal development by organizing documentation, tracking deliverables, and coordinating internal inputs. 
 CRM & Systems Management 
 Own CRM administration, including data structure, workflow automation, and reporting tools. 
 Maintain documentation of sales processes and internal playbooks. 
 Evaluate and implement tools that improve sales productivity and visibility. 
 Operational Support 
 Assist with contract tracking, customer documentation, and deal records. 
 Support on-boarding and enablement of new sales team members. 
 Maintain sales collateral libraries, templates, and standardized documentation. 
 The Candidate 
 We’re looking for individuals with the following traits, skills, and experiences: 
 Bachelors degree in related field is desired. 
 Experience managing CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, or similar). 
 Strong analytical skills and ability to translate data into actionable insights. 
 Highly organized with strong attention to detail. 
 Ability to coordinate across multiple teams and manage competing priorities. 
 Experience in the cleantech or renewable energy industry is required. 
 Why join us? 
 Today, we’re delivering 5x the energy density and have all the certifications needed to ship energy independence to the world. 
 Be part of a mission-driven company focused on creating sustainable energy solutions and making a positive impact on the world. 
 Collaborate closely with passionate co-founders and a team committed to innovation and excellence. 
 Contribute to building and scaling a company from the ground up, where your work will have a direct and meaningful impact. 
 Thrive in a workplace that values collaboration, wellness, and celebrating successes, with regular company socials, fitness sessions, and more. 
 We're a fast-paced and dynamic team. 
 Every day you'll be taking on a new challenge and learning something new. You'll take on a wide breadth of tasks and contribute to disrupting the battery industry. You'll be part of a tight-knit team that is working together to save the planet! Fun, health, and wellness are incorporated into our daily schedule and we encourage all our team members to bring innovative ideas to the table to create an interactive workplace. 
 Moment Energy Benefits Highlights (full time, permanent employees only) 
 Financial Growth: Employee equity and a robust RRSP matching program. 
 Comprehensive Health Coverage: Extended health, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents through Manulife.
 Generous Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off plus a paid company closure between Christmas and New Year's, with a generous paid sick leave.
 Vibrant Culture & Perks: Open and collaborative office culture, frequent company socials and wellness programs (weekly yoga/fitness), and free EV charging on-site.
 Company Dinner: Weekly Tuesday dinner provided by Moment Energy. We also have a generous supply of coffee and snacks for the office! 
 Our Commitments 
 Moment Energy is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection processes, including our work environment. We especially welcome applications from Indigenous peoples, members of racialized communities, persons with disabilities, women, and persons who identify as 2SLGBTQ+. 
 —--- 
 Our Values 
 Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere. We refer to them when we have tough decisions to make, we give shoutouts based on living out these values, and we include them as part of our performance reviews. 
 We have 5 core values and 1 foundational pillar (Safety is our Foundation) which lays the groundwork for everything we do. 
 Safety is our Foundation 
 We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations. Safety is not only about procedures—it is about vigilance, responsibility, and speaking up when something does not feel right. 
 Safety is everyone's responsibility. We follow safety protocols, use proper equipment, and continuously improve our systems to prevent risks before they occur. If something is unsafe, we stop work and address it. 
 Safety also means protecting our colleagues, customers, and communities by designing reliable products, maintaining safe workspaces, and ensuring our work is done carefully and responsibly. 
 We’re Building a Greener Future Together: 
 We infuse passion for our cleantech mission into every aspect of our work and incorporate fun into the workplace. We motivate one another, celebrate our successes and embrace eco-friendly practices to reduce our carbon footprint. 
 We Prioritize our Customer’s Needs: 
 We place our customers at the core of everything we do, ensuring that every decision considers their needs and aims to provide increased value to them. We provide reliable support for our customers, every step of the way. 
 We’re Open, Honest and Accountable: 
 We prioritize open and honest communication to foster mutual understanding, strengthen knowledge sharing, and reduce miscommunication within the team. We admit when we’ve made a mistake, and remedy our actions. We transparently communicate outcomes whether good, bad, or unexpected. 
 We Think and Act like Owners: 
 We’re self-starters that proactively embrace new challenges along with personal and collective ownership of responsibilities in the organization. We focus on growth, not titles, and we do what needs to be done. 
 We Treat Everyone with Respect: 
 We actively listen, share openly, and work together towards common goals. We treat one another with mutual respect to cultivate an inclusive environment where everyone feels accepted, supported, and heard. We keep an open mind and are willing to learn.
